    Important Words
    • ajita — O unconquerable one
      Vocative — Ajita, one of Bhagavān's names (the Unconquered). Mucukunda confesses his wasted time to the very Person no one can conquer. The asymmetry is precisely the point: the confessant addresses the One whose strength makes confession safe.
    • niṣphalaḥ — fruitlessly
      From nis (without) + phala (fruit). His royal years bore no real phala because not offered to Bhagavān. Gauḍīyas read all karma not offered to Kṛṣṇa as phala-less in the ultimate sense — Gītā 9.27 is the cure.
    • rājya-śriyā — by royal opulence
      Compound: rājya (kingdom) + śriyā (opulence). The double intoxication — power and wealth. Vaiṣṇavas note: rājya-śrī is real, but bewildering when not offered to Bhagavān; offered, it becomes Yudhiṣṭhira's rājasūya.
    • martya-ātma-buddheḥ — with mentality of body-as-self
      Compound: martya (mortal body) + ātma (self) + buddheḥ (with intellect identifying). The dehātma-buddhi — the root error Gītā 2 attacks. Mucukunda names it precisely; bhakti requires its dissolution.
    • duranta-cintayā — with endless anxiety
      Compound: duranta (uncrossable) + cintayā (with worry). The interior cost of dehātma-buddhi. Vaiṣṇavas teach that anxiety is structurally inseparable from misidentification — only Bhagavān as refuge ends cintā.
    I have wasted all this time, O unconquerable one, becoming more and more intoxicated by my domain and opulence as an earthly king. Misidentifying the mortal body as the self, becoming attached to children, wives, treasury and land, I suffered endless anxiety.
    Purport

    Having in the previous verse condemned those who misuse the valuable human form of life for mundane purposes, Mucukunda now admits that he himself falls into this category. He intelligently wants to take advantage of the Lord’s association and become a pure devotee once and for all.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    I have wasted all this time, O unconquerable one, becoming more and more intoxicated by my domain and opulence as an earthly king. Misidentifying the mortal body as the self, becoming attached to children, wives, treasury and land, I suffered endless anxiety.
    Commentary

    Who I criticized in the previous verse is actually myself. That is made clear in this verse. I think of the body as the self (martya atma buddheh).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    I am not any different. I have wasted so many yugas. Why? You have not brought people like me under control (ajita). He explains the obstacle to devotion. I have identified myself as a controller of the whole world. Then I became increasingly intoxicated with the wealth of my kingdom. Then I identified with my mortal body and became attached to sons, wife, treasury and land. Then I was overcome with unending worries (duranta-cintayā) about gaining more, as explained in the Gītā. Idam adya mayā labdham: so much have I gained today. (BG 16.13) Or I was overcome with worries from suffering. Not only was my time spent uselessly, but it was full of grief also.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    I have wasted many yugas (eṣaḥ kālaḥ). This is the best time, since you have appeared now (eṣaḥ kālaḥ) but I have wasted it. Or this time at the end of Dvārapā has been wasted. O Lord not under the control of time (ajita)! Or O Lord who has not been controlled by me through bhakti! Thus my time has been wasted. I think I am a king and have become completely intoxicated with domain and wealth. Thus I think I am the body. Or because I think I am the body, I identify as a king and become intoxicated. I am constantly worried about raising children etc. That is described in the following. idam adya mayā labdham: today I have obtained this. (BG 16.13) Or I was overcome with worries ending in suffering. Not only was my time spent uselessly, but it was full of grief also. Or a person like me does not worship your lotus feet. Thus I pass my life uselessly. But not only is it useless because of not worshipping you. It gives suffering because of worrying about the kingdom. I am not any different. I have wasted so many yugas. Why? You have not brought people like me under control (ajita). He explains the obstacle to devotion. I have identified myself as a controller of the whole world. Then I became increasingly intoxicated with the wealth of my kingdom. Then I identified with my mortal body and became attached to sons, wife, treasury and land. Then I was overcome with unending worries (duranta-cintayā) about gaining more, as explained in the Gītā. Idam adya mayā labdham: so much have I gained today. (BG 16.13) Or I was overcome with worries ending in suffering. Not only was my time spent uselessly, but it was full of grief also.

    I have wasted time, intoxicated by domain and opulence as an earthly king — misidentifying the body as self, attached to children, wives, treasury, land, suffering endless anxiety. Confessing past misuse is part of mature devotion.
    Reflection Questions
    • What specific past attachments could you name in honest confession?
    • How does specific confession free what general lament cannot?
    Analogy

    Important Words
    • kalevare — in the body
      Locative of kalevara — body, corpse-shell. The Vaiṣṇava vocabulary refuses to glamorize the body even when alive; it is kalevara already, in essence.
    • ghaṭa-kuḍya-sannibhe — like a pot or a wall
      Compound: ghaṭa (pot) + kuḍya (wall) + sannibhe (resembling). The two stock Vedānta-Vaiṣṇava analogies for material objects. Mucukunda equates his body with them — the diagnostic image for the proper attitude toward the deha.
    • nara-devaḥ — a god among men
      Compound: nara + devaḥ (god). The royal title. Vaiṣṇavas note: only Bhagavān is deva absolutely; the king's nara-deva is courtesy at best, delusion at worst. Mucukunda confesses he took it as the latter.
    • agaṇayan — not regarding seriously
      Present participle of a-√gaṇ — not counting, disregarding. The exact crime of the dehātma-conditioned soul: agaṇayan tvām — disregarding You. The Bhāgavata's force depends on the personal address: not 'ignoring the absolute' but 'disregarding You.'
    • su-durmadaḥ — very much deluded by pride
      Compound: su (very) + durmadaḥ (badly intoxicated). Pride's grammatical superlative. Gauḍīyas read mada (pride) as one of the six ari-ṣaṭ (six inner enemies — verse 57); mada makes Bhagavān invisible because the puffed-up self fills the view.
    With deep arrogance I took myself to be the body, which is a material object like a pot or a wall. Thinking myself a god among men, I traveled the earth surrounded by my charioteers, elephants, cavalry, foot soldiers and generals, disregarding You in my deluding pride.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    With deep arrogance I took myself to be the body, which is a material object like a pot or a wall. Thinking myself a god among men, I traveled the earth surrounded by my charioteers, elephants, cavalry, foot soldiers and generals, disregarding You in my deluding pride.
    Commentary

    I identified with this body which is like a pot or wall (kudya). Because I was so attached to material things, I wasted all my time. This verse is a continuation from the previous verse.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    I took myself to be the body, though it is full of faults. I did not respect you (agaṇayan), since I forgot about you.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    In this body, experienced by everyone as an unconscious object like a pot, or in this body, the shelter of all faults, surrounded by chariots, four parts of the army and generals, I wandered about everywhere on the earth. The later items in the list are closer to the king. I did not respect you (aganayan), since I forgot, being distracted.

    With deep arrogance I took myself to be the body — pot or wall — thinking myself a god, surrounded by charioteers, elephants, cavalry, generals, disregarding You. Pride attaches us to the body's material company.

    Important Words
    • pramattam — thoroughly deluded
      Past participle of pra-√mad — deeply intoxicated. The opposite term to apramattaḥ (later in the verse, applied to Bhagavān). Bhakti's polarity: bhakta apramatta, asura pramatta.
    • viṣayeṣu-lālasam — hankering for sense objects
      Phrase: viṣayeṣu (in sense objects) + lālasam (panting, hungering). Lālasā for viṣaya — the precise direction of misdirected longing. The cure is rāga turned toward Bhagavān (rāgānuga-bhakti).
    • apramattaḥ — ever-alert
      From a (not) + pra-√mad. Bhagavān is structurally apramatta — never inattentive. Gauḍīyas read this as the metaphysics of bhakti's reliability: He never sleeps, never forgets, even when the bhakta does.
    • ahiḥ — a snake
      From √ah — to creep. The image is unsettling on purpose. Bhagavān-as-Time is gentle to bhaktas (gopāla, verse 19) and predatory to the unsurrendered (ahi, verse 49). Same Person, two faces.
    • antakaḥ — death
      From anta — end, plus -ka (agent). The Ender. Gītā 10.34 — 'mṛtyuḥ sarvaharaś cāham' — I am all-snatching Death. The verse here personifies what the Gītā theoretically asserts.
    A man obsessed with thoughts of what he thinks needs to be done, intensely greedy, and delighting in sense enjoyment is suddenly confronted by You, who are ever alert. Like a hungry snake licking its fangs before a mouse, You appear before him as death.
    Purport

    We may note here the contrast between the words pramattam and apramattaḥ. Those who are trying to exploit the material world are pramatta: “deluded, bewildered, maddened by desire.” But the Lord is apramatta: “alert, sober, and unbewildered.” In our madness we may deny God or His laws, but the Lord is sober and will not fail to reward or punish us according to the quality of our activities.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    A man obsessed with thoughts of what he thinks needs to be done, intensely greedy, and delighting in sense enjoyment is suddenly confronted by You, who are ever alert. Like a hungry snake licking its fangs before a mouse, You appear before him as death.
    Commentary

    The lord in the form of time devours those who do not worship him. That is the meaning of this verse. Because the person is attracted to sense objects, he ignores you (pramattah). Thinking that he must do certain actions in the world, he develops ever increasing greed. Even though his desires are frustrated, he is still eager for those objects. You are the destroyer (antakah). With great attention (apramattha), not forgetting about him, as he forgot about you, you overpower him, just as a snake licking his tongue out of hunger, overpowers a mouse.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    This verse describes the ultimate condition of such thoughts. Pramattam means “devoid of attention to the Lord by remembrance etc.” Therefore attachment (lobham) to attained material objects increases and the person cannot desist from enjoying them. He has greed for objects he has not attained (lālasam). Since the Lord causes death through time, he is identified with time (antakaḥ) in the verse. One should worship you out of fear, since you are also the power of time. You approach him suddenly without giving him time to think, coming directly in front of him (abhipadyase). The descriptive terms in the example are general, not making Kṛṣṇa into a snake in all respects.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Though very proud, a man must die. This will happen suddenly. He is completely unaware. But you are aware (apramattaḥ), alert at all times in doing your job. As time you put an end to everything (antakaḥ). Suddenly or beyond logic (sahasā), you cause death (abhipadyase). An example shows the suddenness and alertness: you are like a snake waiting to devour a mouse. Or being completely inattentive to remember you (pramattam ucchaiḥ), increasing greedy for objects, longing for objects incessantly for enjoyment, the person suffers on not attaining them.

    Personal Guidance
    A man obsessed with what 'needs to be done,' intensely greedy, delighting in sense enjoyment, is suddenly confronted by You — ever alert — appearing as death like a hungry snake licking its fangs. The vivid image of death-as-snake corrects illusion of safety.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where are you 'licking fangs' as a snake to your own future?
    • What 'need to be done' might be the very thing distracting you from preparation?
    Analogy

    A man fixated on his to-do list, greed-driven, hungry for sense-pleasure — and Bhagavān comes from behind like a starving snake licking its fangs before a mouse. The image is the Bhāgavata's most striking death-portrait: Kṛṣṇa-as-antaka. Death is not an event; it is a Person.

    Stories
    Kaṁsa hearing the prophecy

    At SB 10.1.34, Kaṁsa hears the asarīrī-voice predict that Devakī's eighth child will be his death. The Bhāgavata-poet describes him exactly as Mucukunda paints the materialist here — pramatta with thoughts of what he must do, greedy, hankering — and Kṛṣṇa, ever-alert, has already begun His descent.

    Gauḍīyas read this parallel pointedly: Kaṁsa's death is Mucukunda's diagnostic. The Lord is, for everyone not surrendered, an antaka eventually. The only escape from the snake-form is to surrender to the snake-handler — Kṛṣṇa Himself in His vatsala-form.

    Important Words
    • rathaiḥ-hema-pariṣkṛtaiḥ — in gold-furnished chariots
      Phrase: rathaiḥ (chariots) + hema (gold) + pariṣkṛtaiḥ (decorated). The kṣatriya-glamour. Vaiṣṇavas use this imagery without scorn — Arjuna's chariot has Kṛṣṇa as charioteer; the issue is not opulence but ownership.
    • nara-deva — king (god among men)
      Same compound as verse 48 — but now used as the past title that bodily decay un-makes. The Bhāgavata's editorial: every nara-deva eventually becomes nara-kalevara, and then less.
    • kālena-duratyayena — by unavoidable time
      Phrase: kālena (by time) + duratyayena (uncrossable). The same kāla of verse 19 — Bhagavān-as-Time. Vaiṣṇavas read this as why kāla cannot be 'managed' from inside saṁsāra: it is the Lord's executive form.
    • viṭ-kṛmi-bhasma-saṁjñitaḥ — named as feces, worms, ashes
      Compound: viṭ (feces) + kṛmi (worms) + bhasma (ashes) + saṁjñitaḥ (named). The body's three terminal forms — buried (worms), exposed (feces, decomposing), cremated (ashes). The verse uses the same bhasma word that named Kālayavana's end (verses 12, 22, 33). Every body shares the asura's exit.
    • kalevaraḥ — the body
      Same word as verse 48 — explicitly chosen to mark the body as already corpse-tending. The whole verse is the kalevara's biography in one breath.
    The body that at first rides high on fierce elephants or chariots adorned with gold and is known by the name “king” is later, by Your invincible power of time, called “feces,” “worms,” or “ashes.”
    Purport

    In the United States and other materially developed countries, dead bodies are cosmetically disposed of in a tidy ceremonial way, but in many parts of the world old, sickly and injured people die in lonely or neglected places, where dogs and jackals consume their bodies and transform them into stool. And if one is so blessed as to be buried in a coffin, one’s body may very well be consumed by worms and other minuscule creatures. Also, many earthly cadavers are burned and thus transformed into ashes. In any case, death is certain, and the ultimate fate of the body is never sublime. That is the real purport of Mucukunda’s statement here — that the body, though now called “king,” “prince,” “beauty queen,” “upper-middle class” and so on, will eventually be called “stool,” “worms” and “ashes.” Śrīla Śrīdhara Svāmī quotes the following Vedic statement: yoneḥ sahasrāṇi bahūni gatvā duḥkhena labdhvāpi ca mānuṣatvam sukhāvahaṁ ye na bhajanti viṣṇuṁ te vai manuṣyātmani śatru-bhūtāḥ “After passing through many thousands of species and undergoing great struggle, the conditioned living entities finally obtain the human form. Thus those human beings who still do not worship Lord Viṣṇu, who can bring them real happiness, have certainly become enemies of both themselves and humanity.”

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The body that at first rides high on fierce elephants or chariots adorned with gold and is known by the name "king" is later, by Your invincible power of time, called "feces," "worms," or "ashes."
    Commentary

    This verse described the body devoured by time. That person who wandered about on a chariot or elephant famous as a king, is devoured by unavoidable death and then takes the disgusting form of stool, worms and ashes.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    In dying the body will take a ghastly form. This is described with disgust. The body which was moving on a chariot becomes ashes etc. by the force of your (te) time. Using the masculine for kalevaram is poetic license. Time cannot be stopped by any means such as sacrifices or yoga (duratyayena) because it is your aṁśa (te).

    Important Words
    • dik-cakram — the whole circle of directions
      Compound: dik (direction) + cakram (wheel, circle). The cakravartī's reach — the conquest of all eight directions. Mucukunda's father Māndhātā was such a cakravartī (SB 9.6); the verse hints at his own dynastic story.
    • vara-āsana-sthaḥ — seated on an exalted throne
      Compound: vara (exalted) + āsana (seat) + sthaḥ (situated). The image of complete worldly arrival. Gauḍīyas read this against the verse's next clause: the same body on the vara-āsana is, in private, krīḍā-mṛga.
    • krīḍā-mṛgaḥ — a pet animal
      Compound: krīḍā (play) + mṛgaḥ (deer, animal). The pet-deer kept for play. The image is precise: the conqueror conquered, the king kinged. Bhakti's diagnosis: external power and internal slavery are the same person.
    • maithunya-sukheṣu — in pleasures of sex
      Compound: maithunya (sexual) + sukheṣu (pleasures). The Bhāgavata names the trap without prudery. Vaiṣṇavas live with this candor: kāma is honored within dharma; outside, it leads. Mucukunda confesses he was led.
    • yoṣitām — of women
      Genitive plural of yoṣit. Not 'women are bad' — but 'whoever is the object of unregulated kāma will be the leash-holder.' Gauḍīyas read this against Vraja-mādhurya: the gopīs are not yoṣit-snares but Bhagavān's own hlādinī-śakti, structurally different.
    Having conquered the entire circle of directions and being thus free of conflict, a man sits on a splendid throne, receiving praise from leaders who were once his equals. But when he enters the women’s chambers, where sex pleasure is found, he is led about like a pet animal, O Lord.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Having conquered the entire circle of directions and being thus free of conflict, a man sits on a splendid throne, receiving praise from leaders who were once his equals. But when he enters the women's chambers, where sex pleasure is found, he is led about like a pet animal, O Lord.
    Commentary

    In the previous verse it was stated that a person who achieved kingly status among his peers ends up as stool and worms by the force of time at the end of life. This verse describes how, during the present life, a person who achieves kingly status becomes like a pet animal in the hands of women. Having freed himself of conflicts, he is worshipped by kings who were once his equals. He is made to move about like a pet animal in the inner chambers of the women for sexual pleasure, by those women or their servants.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    There is no happiness at death for a person who has lived a life of enjoyment. Even in being a king with all enjoyment one suffers because of dependence. This is explained in two verses. Though situated on a great throne, he is led by women, and even their female servants. O Lord, this happens because they are all subject to your māyā.

    Personal Guidance
    Free of conflict, sitting on a splendid throne receiving praise — but in the women's chambers led about like an ox by a chain in his nose. Even great rulers are led by base desires; status doesn't free anyone from basic compulsions.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where in your private chambers are you led like an ox while publicly enthroned?
    • How do you reconcile public dignity with private compulsion?
    Analogy

    A king who has conquered every direction sits on a glittering throne, praised by his equals — and is then led like a pet into the women's chambers, by hands no army could resist. The verse's pivot: external conquest, internal subjugation. The truly free man is the one Mucukunda is becoming.

    Important Words
    • tapaḥ-su-niṣṭhitaḥ — very fixed in austerity
      Compound: tapaḥ (austerity) + su (very) + niṣṭhitaḥ (steady). Mucukunda concedes the materialist's tapas can be intense — but it is in service of bhūyāsam ('greater I'), and so fails. Gauḍīyas read this as the structural argument for bhakti over jñāna-tapas.
    • nivṛtta-bhogaḥ — abstaining from sense enjoyment
      Compound: nivṛtta (turned-away) + bhogaḥ (enjoyment). Real abstention, not pretended. But pointed at the wrong telos — self-aggrandizement — it does not yield happiness. Bhakti's frame: abstention must serve Bhagavān, not the future-greater-self.
    • sva-rāṭ — sovereign, self-ruler
      Compound: sva (own) + rāṭ (king). The fatal thought — 'I am my own king.' Gauḍīyas read sva-rāṭ-illusion as the structural opposite of dāsa-bhāva (servant-mood); they are mutually exclusive.
    • pravṛddha-tarṣaḥ — with rampant urges
      Compound: pravṛddha (grown, rampant) + tarṣaḥ (thirst, longing). The interior state under the sva-rāṭ thought. Tapas suppresses; tarṣa returns. Only bhakti transmutes.
    • na-sukhāya-kalpate — cannot attain happiness
      Phrase: sukhāya (for happiness) + na kalpate (does not lead). The verdict. Vaiṣṇavas treasure this verse as scriptural ground for the insufficiency of niṣkāma-karma without bhakti — Kṛṣṇa Himself articulates this in Gītā 6.47.
    A king who desires even greater power than he already has strictly performs his duties, carefully practicing austerity and forgoing sense enjoyment. But he whose urges are so rampant, thinking “I am independent and supreme,” cannot attain happiness.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    A king who desires even greater power than he already has strictly performs his duties, carefully practicing austerity and forgoing sense enjoyment. But he whose urges are so rampant, thinking "I am independent and supreme," cannot attain happiness.
    Commentary

    The man who does not worship the lord is condemned for his enjoyment of worldly pleasures. But the same man is condemned even when he lacks his material enjoyment. He is fixed in austerities such as sleeping on the ground and observing celibacy, with the urge to become an even more powerful king, or even Indra himself.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Though following dharma and expecting a happy after life, a person only encounters suffering. A person engages in activities like sacrifices and vows because of being fixed in austerity. Though he renounces enjoyment, he performs his charities etc with expectation of enjoyment, or he gives donations as a part of his pious karmas. In doing so he suffers because of depletion of material wealth in this life. And he is not qualified for happiness even in after life, for he must fear falling from that position. Kṣayiṣṇor nāsti nirvṛttiḥ: there is no happiness in what is temporary. (Viṣṇu Purāṇa) deva-loka-gatiṁ prāpto nātha deva-gaṇo 'pi hi / mattaḥ sāhāyya kāmo ‘bhūc chāśvatī kutra nirvṛtiḥ // O Lord! Even the devatās who attained the goal of Svarga desired help from me (Mucukunda). Where is the eternal happiness? Viṣṇu Purāṇa

    Concepts
    Dharma
    Personal Guidance
    A king desiring greater power strictly performs duties, practices austerity, forgoes sense enjoyment; but he whose urges are rampant — 'I am independent and supreme' — cannot attain happiness. Discipline serves ambition more reliably than indulgence.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where do you indulge urges and call it freedom while losing the very happiness you seek?
    • What disciplines would actually serve your higher ambition?
    Analogy

    A king who wants more power performs penance, regulates senses — and the moment he thinks 'I am sovereign,' his urges roar back. The Bhāgavata's diagnosis: tapas without bhakti is a deferred kāma, not an extinguished one. Self-effort without surrender does not deliver peace.

    Important Words
    • bhava-apavargaḥ — the cessation of material existence
      Compound: bhava (becoming, samsāra) + apavargaḥ (cessation). The end of wandering. Gauḍīyas note: apavarga here does not mean Advaitin merging; it means saṁsāra ending so that bhakti can begin. Liberation in the Gauḍīya frame is service, not absorption.
    • sat-samāgamaḥ — the association of saintly devotees
      Compound: sat (saintly, real) + samāgamaḥ (meeting). The Vaiṣṇava's catalyst — sādhu-saṅga, sat-saṅga. Caitanya-caritāmṛta repeatedly cites this verse; Rūpa Gosvāmī ranks sādhu-saṅga first among bhakti's nourishments.
    • acyuta — O infallible Lord
      Vocative of Acyuta — He who does not fall. One of Bhagavān's primary names. Mucukunda addresses Kṛṣṇa as Acyuta precisely at the verse about falling — saṁsāric falling, devotee non-falling. The vocative is doctrinal.
    • sat-gatau — the goal of the saintly
      Compound: sat + gatau (goal, destination). Bhagavān as the bhakta's destination. Gauḍīyas read this against impersonalist destinations — sat-gati is a Person, not a state.
    • matiḥ — devotion, fixed intelligence
      From √man — to think. Here, the buddhi turned toward Bhagavān. Same matiḥ that was 'asat-mati' in verse 46 is now bhakti-mati. The chapter rotates the same word.
    When the material life of a wandering soul has ceased, O Acyuta, he may attain the association of Your devotees. And when he associates with them, there awakens in him devotion unto You, who are the goal of the devotees and the Lord of all causes and their effects.
    Purport

    Ācāryas Jīva Gosvāmī and Viśvanātha Cakravartī agree on the following point: Although it is stated here that when material life ceases one attains the association of devotees, in fact it is the association of the Lord’s devotees that enables one to transcend material existence. Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī explains this apparent inversion of sequence by quoting the Kāvya-prakāśa (10.153) as follows: kārya-kāraṇayoś ca paurvāparya-viparyayo vijñeyātiśayoktiḥ syāt sa. “A statement in which the logical order of a cause and its effect is reversed should be understood as atiśayokti, emphasis by extreme assertion.” Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī cites the following commentary on this statement: kāraṇasya śīghra-kārītāṁ vaktuṁ kāryasya pūrvam uktau. “To express the swift action of a cause, one may assert the result before the cause.” In this connection Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī points out that the merciful association of the Lord’s devotees makes possible our determination to become Kṛṣṇa conscious. And the ācārya agrees with Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī that this verse is an instance of atiśayokti.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    When the material life of a wandering soul has ceased, O Acyuta, he may attain the association of Your devotees. And when he associates with them, there awakens in him devotion unto You, who are the goal of the devotees and the Lord of all causes and their effects.
    Commentary

    When will bhakti which destroys all suffering and bestows all bliss appear? That is stated in this verse. When the wandering jiva destroys his bondage of material existence, then he will get association of merciful devotees (sat sangamah). When that happens, then certainly attachment to you will take place. When that association occurs, and nothing else, then attachment to you will take place. In this verse the words "when" and "then" is used with a broad conception of time. In the concept of more accurate time, however, association of devotees and destruction of material existence are related as cause and effect and should be mentioned in that way, using yarhi and tarhi; that is, when there is association of devotees, then there is destruction of bondage. However, because the effect happens so quickly, the effect is mentioned before the cause, to emphasize the quickness. This is an example of the fourth type of atisaya ukti or extreme statement. Vaisnava tosani explains the word sad gatau. Unto you the shelter of the devotees. "Without my mercy association does not take place. Therefore my mercy should be the first cause. " "When there is devotional association, then attachment to you whose shelter is the devotee (who is dependent on the devotee, gives mercy to the devotee) arises. As you yourself say, I am dependent on the devotee, whatever you do is also by the desire of the devotee, it Is not independent. Your mercy is after the mercy of the devotee. You are dependent on the devotee, and not dependent on the non devotee. The later state your mercy arises from the previous state, devotee’s mercy. Therefore your mercy does not arise first. Such mercy of the devotees is shown in the statement 10.23.31. svayam samuttirya...The great devotees who take shelter of your feet cross over the ocean of material existence, and leave here through the line of guru succession the boat of your lotus feet, because they are most affectionate to all living entities."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    When will that person attain auspiciousness? When those with knowledge attain liberation, then the discerning persons attain association. Or it can be the fourth type of literary ornament called atiśayokti. Caturthī sā kāraṇasya gaditam śīghra-kārītāṁ vaktuṁ kāryasya pūrvam uktau: the fourth type is that in order to express the swift action of a cause, one may assert the result before the cause.” Thus the real meaning is “Where there is association with devotees, there is quick release from saṁsāra, because, where there is association, one is able to fix one’s mind on you.” Where one concentrates the mind on you, there will be certain release from samṣāra, at that time only (eva) and no other time. O Lord, you never fail to do this (acyuta)! “Without my mercy there can be no association with devotees. Let my mercy be the first cause.” The Lord takes shelter (gatau) of the devotees (sat). Though he is independent, his mercy occurs by the will of the devotees, not independently. Aham bhakta-parādhinaḥ: I am dependent on my devotees. (SB 9.4. 63) The mercy follows the devotee. You are dependent on the devotees, not on the non-devotees. Only when there is prior association of devotees does mercy occur, and not before that. svayaṁ samuttīrya sudustaraṁ dyuman bhavārṇavaṁ bhīmam adabhra-sauhṛdāḥ bhavat-padāmbhoruha-nāvam atra te nidhāya yātāḥ sad-anugraho bhavān O Lord, shining brilliantly! The merciful devotees, easily crossing the insurmountable and terrifying ocean of material life, attain their goal using the boat of your lotus feet. You are merciful to your devotees. SB 10.2.31 Thus by association of devotees alone, the mind concentrates on you. This is because you are not dependent on what higher or lower beings (parāvareśe) know. By association with Garga, I have been able to fix my mind on you. You have said, “Since in the past you repeatedly prayed to me, I have personally come to this cave to show you mercy.” (verse 42) Because of that, I have now attained you, the giver of freedom from saṁsāra. Instead of mati sometimes ratiḥ is seen. The bud of rati, concentration on the Lord, arises by association alone.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    When or if saṁsāra is destroyed, association with your devotees occurs. The potential form (bhavet) expresses possibility. You are unfailing in your persistence. Or when there is rejection of family life association arises. Or when there is liberation in Vaikuṇṭha there is association with the devotees (sat) of you (acyuta) or with devotees who never fall (acyuta). Or there is steady association with devotees. At that time alone, or exactly at that moment, one develops devotion to you. This is because the Lord is attained through the devotees (sad-gatau). Thus the Lord says na rodhayati māṁ yogaḥ: yoga does not attract me. (SB 11.12.1) Why is this? You are the attained by bhakti which derides (avara) liberation (para). Or though you are the lord of all higher and lower beings (parāvareśe), you take shelter of devotees (sad-gatau). Sometimes rati is seen instead of bhakti. There will occur rati for you by steady association with devotees after destruction of saṁsāra.

    • Romapada Sw SB 10-51-53 - Vyasa Puja - 2014-01-18 ISKCON Chicago
      His Holiness Romapada Swami· 2014-01-18· English
    Personal Guidance
    When material life of a wandering soul ceases, he may attain the association of Your devotees; and from that, devotion to You — the goal of devotees, Lord of all causes — awakens. The path is sequential: ceasing material life, sangha, devotion.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where could you accelerate the cessation phase enough to enter sangha?
    • Which devotional company might be the next on-ramp?
    Analogy

    When the long wandering ends, the soul meets devotees — and from that meeting, bhakti to Bhagavān is born. The verse names the exact mechanism: sādhu-saṅga is the catalyst. Mucukunda gives a chapter-long stuti in the form of a theology of how Vaiṣṇavas come into being.

    Stories
    Nārada's previous birth (SB 1.5-6)

    Nārada, in his earlier birth as the son of a maidservant, served the caraṇas (wandering sages) during a single rainy season. The remnants of their food, their company, and their songs created the seed of his bhakti. He says in SB 1.5.25-26 that all the saṁskāras of his next life — his Nārada-vapu, his vīṇā, his perpetual kṛṣṇa-kīrtana — flowed from that one rainy-season sādhu-saṅga.

    Gauḍīyas read Nārada's story as the exact illustration of Mucukunda's verse 53. The wandering ends, sādhu-saṅga begins, bhakti is born. The chapter pivots on this verse — every reader of Bhāgavatam at this moment is invited to recognize themselves as the bhramat-jana (wandering soul) the verse names.

    Important Words
    • anugrahaḥ — mercy
      Same word as verse 42 — Kṛṣṇa's stated motive comes back as Mucukunda's recognition. The chapter rotates anugraha through the Lord's mouth and the devotee's mouth — same word, mutual acknowledgment.
    • rājya-anubandha-apagamaḥ — the removal of attachment to kingdom
      Compound: rājya + anubandha (binding) + apagamaḥ (departure). Mucukunda names the precise gift — not the kingdom's removal (it had already gone), but the binding-to-kingdom's departure. Bhakti's discrimination.
    • yadṛcchayā — spontaneously
      Adverb — by Bhagavān's wish, without effort. Vaiṣṇavas insist that the deepest detachment is yadṛcchā — not earned, but given. Bhakti is structurally a gift, not an attainment.
    • eka-caryayā — by living alone
      Compound: eka (alone) + caryayā (by conduct). The solitary forest-life that great kings pray to enter. Mucukunda has been given its fruit without having to enter it. Bhagavān shortcuts.
    • akhaṇḍa-bhūmi-paiḥ — by rulers of unbroken lands
      Compound: akhaṇḍa (unbroken, vast) + bhūmi (lands) + paiḥ (rulers). The cakravartīs — Yudhiṣṭhira, Bharata, Pṛthu, Khaṭvāṅga, Māndhātā. Mucukunda places himself in their fellowship, claiming the same prayer-content. Vaiṣṇava lineage of detached kings.
    My Lord, I think You have shown me mercy, since my attachment to my kingdom has spontaneously ceased. Such freedom is prayed for by saintly rulers of vast empires who desire to enter the forest for a life of solitude.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    My Lord, I think You have shown me mercy, since my attachment to my kingdom has spontaneously ceased. Such freedom is prayed for by saintly rulers of vast empires who desire to enter the forest for a life of solitude.
    Commentary

    "That I gave up attachment to kingdom and other things after association with your devotees is your mercy." That is expressed in this verse. Vrtrasura said, " O indra, my master the Lord is the destroy of all attempts at dharma artha and kama for his devotees. By that one can infer his mercy. Such mercy is only available to the selfless devotees of the Lord. It cannot be attained by those attached to material energy." This mercy, destruction of attachment to kingdom, is prayed for attentively, as an uninterrupted meditation on you to perfect devotion, by saintly kings.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Starting from association, you have shown me mercy. O Lord, skillful at doing the impossible, like making the mute person eloquent! Attachment to y kingdom has ceased. This is because of your mercy. I think it has been done by you by your free will (yadṛcchayā). This mercy is sought by those fixed only on you, even by rulers of the world, what to speak of rulers of part of Bharata-varṣa. Why do they want to retire to the forest? They have given up thinking of material things by discrimination (sādhubhiḥ).

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    I think that you have been merciful to me. Why? Without effort, attachment to my kingdom or pursuit of material objects has ceased. You have shown mercy by which attachment has ceased. O Lord, you can do this because you have the power or you have done this because I am not capable of doing it. That mercy is requested by the highest devotees (ekacaryayā), even having a wealth of enjoyment (akhaṇḍa-bhūmi-paiḥ), though this usually disqualifies one for higher intelligence. Or that mercy is requested by the highest devotees even if they own the whole world, what to speak of owning a part of it. Why do they desire the forest? They are devotees (sādhubhiḥ).

    I think You've shown me mercy, since my attachment to my kingdom has spontaneously ceased — the freedom kings pray for to enter forest life. When attachment falls off without effort, recognize it as the Lord's mercy.
    Reflection Questions
    • What attachment has recently 'spontaneously ceased' for you, and have you thanked Him?
    • Where do you over-explain a release that simply was given?
    Analogy

    Mucukunda confesses the gift: his attachment to kingdom has fallen off by itself. What great kings pray for after years of forest-retreat, Kṛṣṇa has bestowed in a cave-meeting. Detachment as Bhagavān's prasāda, not as the bhakta's achievement.

    Stories
    King Bharata's renunciation

    King Bharata, the cakravartī after whom the land is named, renounced his vast empire in his prime and entered the forest to pursue bhakti (SB 5.7-8). Even then, he became attached to a deer and had to be re-incarnated as a brāhmaṇa (Jaḍa Bharata) to complete his journey.

    Gauḍīyas read Mucukunda's verse 54 as the easier path: rather than walking away from rājya himself, he received Kṛṣṇa's darśana, and rājya walked away from him. Spontaneous detachment via grace is the bhakti-path; effort-detachment via forest-renunciation is the sannyāsa-path. The chapter prefers the first.

    Important Words
    • pāda-sevanāt — than service to (Your) feet
      Compound: pāda + sevanāt (than service). Pāda-sevanam is one of bhakti's nine limbs (SB 7.5.23). The bhakta wants this specific bhakti — service of the lotus feet — and refuses everything else.
    • akiñcana — by those who want nothing material
      Compound: a (not) + kiñcana (anything). The akiñcanas are Bhagavān's dearest. Akiñcana-vitta — the wealth of having nothing — is the Bhāgavata's signature value. Caitanya prayed: 'na dhanaṁ na janaṁ na sundarīṁ.'
    • varam-ātma-bandhanam — a boon (causing one's own) bondage
      Phrase: varam (boon) + ātma (self) + bandhanam (bondage). The deep insight — any boon except service binds. Gauḍīyas treasure this verse for its uncompromising clarity: material boons are bondage masquerading as gifts.
    • apavarga-dam — the bestower of liberation
      Compound: apavarga (liberation) + dam (bestower). The same apavarga of verse 53. Bhagavān can give liberation — but the bhakta does not even want it; he wants service. Gauḍīyas distinguish apavarga from premā-bhakti and prefer the second.
    • āryaḥ — a spiritually advanced person
      From ṛ-root — noble, refined, spiritually advanced. Mucukunda invokes the category of the ārya as the one who refuses bondage-boons. The Vaiṣṇava ārya is defined by what he refuses to accept.
    O all-powerful one, I desire no boon other than service to Your lotus feet, the boon most eagerly sought by those free of material desire. O Hari, what enlightened person who worships You, the giver of liberation, would choose a boon that causes his own bondage?
    Purport

    The Lord offered Mucukunda anything he desired, but Mucukunda desired only the Lord. This is pure Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    O all-powerful one, I desire no boon other than service to Your lotus feet, the boon most eagerly sought by those free of material desire. O Hari, what enlightened person who worships You, the giver of liberation, would choose a boon that causes his own bondage?
    Commentary

    You have said "Ask for a benediction." I answer with this verse. Those who are akincana pray for bhakti. More worthy of prayer is prema. Most worthy of prayer is to serve your lotus feet. Thus I do not want liberation, what to speak of any other boon. Here apavarga da, referring to the Lord, means he who gives bhakti yoga. , as in the use of the word in the fifth canto of bhagavatam. Can an intelligent person after worshipping you who gives bhakti, accept boons which bind him to the word, even if you give them? Another meaning can be: even one who worships and gets liberation from you, if he is intelligent, can he accept your boons which create bondage to the world again? What to speak then of the devotee.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    I do not desire anything for getting blessings other than service to your lotus feet, by direct engagements. I desire only that. Why? It is desired by the devotees who regard even liberation as insignificant (akiṣcana). They pray for bhakti. More than that, they pray to see you. And more than that, they pray for service to your lotus feet. It is greater than all other human goals. He calls out for qualification. O powerful lord, capable of bestowing happiness of all human goals (vibho)! Worshipping or attaining you (ārādhya), who gives bhakti (apavarga), what person would accept bondage? Apavarga means bhakti as in the following: apavargaś cāpi bhavati yo 'sau bhagavati sarva-bhūtātmany anātmye 'nirukte 'nilayane paramātmani vāsudeve 'nanya-nimitta-bhakti-yoga-lakṣaṇo nānā-gati-nimittāvidyā-granthi-randhana-dvāreṇa yadā hi mahā-puruṣa-puruṣa-prasaṅgaḥ. That liberation, whose essential nature is unmotivated bhakti-yoga to the Lord full of qualities, who attracts the minds of all beings, who is not the object of merging, who is not described by material words, who remains beyond destruction of the universe, who is the most excellent ātmā, who is the son of Vasudeva, takes place by destruction of the knot of ignorance which causes various material goals, when there is association with devotees of the Lord. SB 5.19.19-20 Or apavarga means liberation. Why do you not accept liberation? Worshipping or serving you who are permanent with some affection, what person can accept a benediction which gives mere liberation? Accepting that benediction is a cause of bondage.

      Her Grace Urmila Mataji· 2024-05-13· English
    Personal Guidance
    I desire no boon other than service to Your lotus feet — sought by those free of material desire. What enlightened person would choose a boon causing his own bondage? The mature devotee specifies the ask is service, not items.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where does your current asking still risk causing your own bondage?
    • Could the next request you make be specifically for service?
    Analogy

    Mucukunda's central petition: 'I want nothing but service at Your lotus feet. What enlightened person, worshiping You who give liberation, would choose his own bondage?' The verse is the chapter's pivot from request to refusal — and from refusal to the highest request.

    Stories
    Dhruva's regret

    Dhruva Mahārāja, in SB 4.9, performs years of intense tapas seeking a kingdom greater than his father's, meets Viṣṇu, and afterward laments — 'I came for pieces of glass; You showed me the cintāmaṇi. What a fool I was.' The same realization animates Mucukunda's verse 55: any boon less than service is the bhakta's own bondage-request.

    Gauḍīyas read both verses together as the structural argument for niṣkāma-bhakti. The devotee who knows what Bhagavān actually is cannot ask Him for anything else. Asking for boons is the diagnostic of not-yet-knowing.

    Important Words
    • puruṣam-vrajāmi — I approach the Person
      Phrase — 'You, the puruṣa, I approach.' The technical śaraṇāgati formula. Echoes Gītā 18.66 (mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja). Gauḍīyas treasure this verse as the Bhāgavata's parallel śaraṇāgati-mantra.
    • nirañjanam — free from mundane designations
      From nir (without) + añjana (smudge, designation). Bhagavān untouched by upādhis. Gauḍīyas distinguish this from Māyāvāda nirañjana: Bhagavān is nirañjana as to mundane labels, but full of His own transcendental form, name, qualities.
    • nirguṇam — transcendental to the material modes
      From nir + guṇa. Bhagavān is nirguṇa with respect to prakṛti-guṇas (sattva-rajas-tamas) but eternally full of transcendental guṇas (sat-cit-ānanda). The Gauḍīya distinction is critical: nirguṇa ≠ attributeless.
    • advayam — nondual
      From a (not) + dvaya (two). Gauḍīyas read advaya not as Advaitin monism but as Bhagavān's status as the unrivaled absolute — there is no second to Him because He encompasses His own energies (acintya-bhedābheda).
    • jñāpti-mātram — pure knowledge
      Compound: jñāpti (knowing) + mātram (only, pure). Bhagavān as cit-svarūpa — pure consciousness. But again, not impersonal consciousness; consciousness-as-Person. The mātra here means 'fully,' not 'merely.'
    • puruṣam — the original Person
      The chapter's most loaded word, repeated through the stuti. After listing the nir- and a- prefixes (negations), Mucukunda anchors with puruṣam — the affirmative Personalist note. All negations terminate in this Person.
    Therefore, O Lord, having put aside all objects of material desire, which are bound to the modes of passion, ignorance and goodness, I am approaching You, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, for shelter. You are not covered by mundane designations; rather, You are the Supreme Absolute Truth, full in pure knowledge and transcendental to the material modes.
    Purport

    The word nirguṇam here indicates that the Lord’s existence is beyond the qualities of material nature. One might argue that Lord Kṛṣṇa’s body is made of material nature, but here the word advayam refutes that argument. There is no duality in Lord Kṛṣṇa’s existence. His eternal, spiritual body is Kṛṣṇa, and Kṛṣṇa is God.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Therefore, O Lord, having put aside all objects of material desire, which are bound to the modes of passion, ignorance and goodness, I am approaching You, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, for shelter. You are not covered by mundane designations; rather, You are the Supreme Absolute Truth, full in pure knowledge and transcendental to the material modes.
    Commentary

    In this veres Mucukunda clarifies his desirelessness for all objects of the world. Having given up relation with sattva raja and tama gunas, I also give up liberation related to sattva guna, which causes jnana. I pray for bhakti which consists of service to your lotus feet, which is beyond the three gunas. The eleventh chapter of Gita states that bhakti is beyond the three modes. I attain (vrajami) you, as a person (purusam). "But some say that my form as a person is brahman covered by maya. "No, you are without the gunas, nirguna, without covering (niranjana). " "Yes I may be without gunas, but some people say that my body is made of the gunas." "You and your body are not different (advayam). You are your body." "What is the nature of that body?" "It is cit svarupa, Brahman (jnapti matram)." Another meaning: "Because the world is made of your energy, it is not different from you advaya. But you by your svarupa sakti are a body of pure knowledge."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    I reject all results (aśiśaḥ) completely, even liberation, which are contrary to serving your feet. Even jṣāna is in sattva and therefore a cause of bondage. Service to your feet however is beyond the guṇas. sāttviky ādhyātmikī śraddhā karma-śraddhā tu rājasī tāmasy adharme yā śraddhā mat-sevāyāṁ tu nirguṇā Faith in ātmā is in sattva, faith in prescribed karma is in rajas, faith in irreligious activities is in tamas, but faith in my devotional service is beyond the guṇas. SB 11.25.27 I surrender to you the Lord (puruṣam), the form of condensed knowledge (jṣaptimātram), since you are spotless, because you are beyond the guṇas (nirguṇam), since you are advayam. I surrender to you, Svayam Bhagavān, who have appeared in this form before me. This meaning is consistent with other statements in Bhāgavatam. Satyaṁ paraṁ dhīmahi: I meditate upon the Lord known as Satya. (SB 1.1.1) Kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam: of all the forms mentioned Kṛṣṇa is the perfect manifestation of all qualities. (SB 1.3.28) Ādyo ‘vatāraḥ puruṣaḥ parasya: Mahā-viṣṇu is an expansion of the Lord in the spiritual sky. (SB 2.6.82) atha vā bahunaitena kiṁ jṣātena tavārjuna | viṣṭabhyāham idaṁ kṛtsnam ekāṁśena sthito jagat ||42|| But what is the use of knowing all these individual vibhūtis, Arjuna? Please understand: by just one portion of Myself, I am firmly established in this universe. BG 10.42 According to Gītā the antaryāmī is known as Paramātmā: tvāṁ yogino yajanty addhā mahā-puruṣam īśvaram sādhyātmaṁ sādhibhūtaṁ ca sādhidaivaṁ ca sādhavaḥ Pure yogīs worship you, the Supreme Lord, by conceiving of you in the threefold form comprising the living entities, the material elements that constitute the living entities’ bodies, and the controlling deities of those elements. SB 10.40.4 Kṛṣṇa is jṣapti-mātram or the Brahman spread everywhere as consciousness alone: jṣāna-mātraṁ paraṁ brahma paramātmeśvaraḥ pumān dṛśy-ādibhiḥ pṛthag bhāvair bhagavān eka īyate The one form of Bhagavān also perceived as Brahman, consciousness alone, and as Paramātmā, the puruṣa, by differing practices performed by different practitioners. SB 3.32.26 vadanti tat tattva-vidas tattvaṁ yaj jṣānam advayam | brahmeti paramātmeti bhagavān iti śabdyate || The knowers of truth call this truth advayam-jṣānam, the supreme conscious being, who is called brahman by the jṣānīs, Paramātmā by the yogīs and Bhagavān by the devotees. SB 1.2.11 You are beyond māyā in these three forms. You are without upādhis (niraṣjanam), situated in your svarūpa with no coverings. As Bhagavān and Paramātmā you are without qualities—beyond the material guṇas but having spiritual qualities which are part of your svarūpa (nirguṇam). māṁ bhajanti guṇāḥ sarve nirguṇaṁ nirapekṣakam suhṛdaṁ priyam ātmānaṁ sāmyāsaṅgādayo ’guṇāḥ All superior qualities, which are eternal, such as equality to all beings and attachment to my devotee, reside in me. I am beyond the material guṇas, not dependent on material qualities, and am the devotees’ friend, giving love to them. SB 11.13.40 You have no one equal or superior to you and nothing different from you (advayam). Though you are consciousness alone, your svarūpa-śakti can be realized since it is the nature of the Lord. Īkṣater nāśabdam: the Lord is expressed through words. (Brahma-sūtra 1.1.5) According to the commentary he who is knowledge personified does not need jṣāna-sādhana for realization. His very nature is revelation. Therefore he does not depend on a sādhana to be revealed. The scriptures clearly state this in regards to Bhagavān and Paramātmā. na tasya kāryam karaṇaṁ ca vidyate na tat samaś cābhyadhikaśca dṛśyate parāsya śaktir vivdhaiva śruyate svābhāvikī jṣana-bala-kriya ca He has no body and no senses. No one is equal to him or higher. His supreme power is manifold. His actions are naturally revealed with knowledge and strength. Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad Apāṇipādo javano grahītā He is without hands and feet but quickly accepts what is offered. Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasyaiṣa ātmā vṛṇute tanuṁ svām || The Lord reveals his form to whomsoever he chooses. Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 3.2.4 Or, he is completely attractive (niraṣjanam). He increases (guṇayati) unlimitedly with distribution of bhakti. He is without rivals (advayam). One of his portions (mātram) is Brahman (jṣapti). You are eternity knowledge and bliss, with unlimited śaktis in a human form. I approach you as my object of service (vrajāmi).

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    I reject all results (aśiśaḥ) completely, even liberation, which are contrary to serving your feet. Even jṣāna is in sattva and therefore a cause of bondage. I surrender to your alone (advayam). Why? You are the supreme lord (param puruṣam) or the supreme person. Therefore you have unlimited qualities (nirguṇam) or you expand unlimitedly by spreading bhakti. Therefore you are continually attractive (niraṣjanam). Since you are pure knowledge, you are awareness itself, with no dependence on another source of knowledge. I approach you. Let others accept other results. O I have great longing for a long time. “I cannot give that for which you take shelter of me.” You are capable of giving everything (īśa). Or you know more than what is to be known from other sources (jṣapti-mātram). You can give more than what is requested (īśa).

    Having put aside material objects bound by the modes, I approach You for shelter — You are not covered by mundane designations; You are pure being beyond all qualities. The Lord's transcendence is the actual shelter.

    O Lord .
    Important Words
    • vṛjina-ārtaḥ — distressed by troubles
      Compound: vṛjina (suffering) + ārtaḥ (distressed). The diagnostic state preceding śaraṇāgati. Gītā 7.16 catalogues four types of pious surrenderers; ārta is the first.
    • ṣaṭ-amitraḥ — the six enemies
      Compound: ṣaṭ (six) + amitraḥ (enemies). The classical ari-ṣaṭ — kāma, krodha, lobha, mada, moha, mātsarya. Six inner asuras that no outer victory subdues. Only bhakti subdues them — the Vaiṣṇava ethics implicit in the verse.
    • śaraṇa-da — O bestower of shelter
      Compound: śaraṇa (shelter) + da (bestower). Bhagavān's defining vocative in the moment of surrender. Gauḍīyas read this as the technical name for the act being performed — śaraṇa-grahaṇa, taking refuge.
    • para-ātman — O Supreme Soul
      Compound: para (supreme) + ātman (soul). Bhagavān as Paramātman — distinct from the jīva-ātman. Gauḍīyas firmly distinguish: jīva-ātma serves; Paramātma is served. Mucukunda's vocative honors the distinction.
    • pada-abjam — lotus feet
      Compound: pada + abjam (water-born, lotus). The same lotus feet of verse 27 — Mucukunda's first concern in the chapter, his final refuge here. The image arcs across the stuti.
    • abhayam — fearless, free of fear
      From a (not) + bhayam (fear). Bhagavān's lotus feet are abhaya. Gītā 18.66's promise — mā śucaḥ — is here read backward from the bhakta's side: the feet that grant abhaya are the feet I have approached.
    For so long I have been pained by troubles in this world and have been burning with lamentation. My six enemies are never satiated, and I can find no peace. Therefore, O giver of shelter, O Supreme Soul, please protect me. O Lord, in the midst of danger I have by good fortune approached Your lotus feet, which are the truth and which thus make one fearless and free of sorrow.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    For so long I have been pained by troubles in this world and have been burning with lamentation. My six enemies are never satiated, and I can find no peace. Therefore, O giver of shelter, O Supreme Soul, please protect me. O Lord, in the midst of danger I have by good fortune approached Your lotus feet, which are the truth and which thus make one fearless and free of sorrow.
    Commentary

    "First you can enjoy all objects worthy of enjoyment, and then I will give you service to my feet. " Fearing such enticement from Krsna, Mucukunda offers this praye. Being afflicted by miseries, in the conflict with Indra’s enemies desiring victory, burning with repentence, such as "for so many days I have not worshipped the Lord," with no cessation of the desire for enjoyment of the six senses of eye, ear, nose tongue and skin and mind, I do not get peace either by my own intelligence or by knowledge given by others. If enjoyment is given by you yourself, even then I will become entangled. That is the nature of enjoyment. Therefore do not give that enjoyment. O paramatma, who resides in everyone, who therefore knows everything, I have taken Your lotus feet. In material treasure, there is fear of sickness, and enemies etc. In heavenly treusure there is impermanence. In the treasure of Brahman one is cheated of service to your lotus feet. Bur the treasure of your feet are without fear (abhayam), without impermanence (nrtam) and without lamentation (asokam). Therefore protect me, who am afflicted with calamity. Protect me at your lotus feet."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Now you should not disregard me. Protect me completely. He speaks with humility. Suffering from the experience of sins in saṁsāra (iha) for a long time, suffering from lamentation after exhaustion of pious results, I have not attained peace or steadiness of heart (happiness) by any means. Or, I have not attained peace by any cause discernable without effort, by any cause which can be directly perceived. I have come close to you (samupetaḥ). The Lord’s suitability is described. O giver of shelter! You give shelter according to your promise. Ārtānāṁ śaraṇaṁ tv aham: I am the shelter for the sufferers. (SB 11.26.33) You should not say that shelter is dependent on bhakti to you since you are the inspiration for bhakti. Parātman! You should give what is according to the glory of your lotus feet and nothing else. He describes Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet with three descriptive phrases: they are free from sorrow, free from fear and full of truth. Please protect me, by engaging me in service, since you are affectionate to the fallen. In humility he again speaks. I am surrendered. You alone can do this (īśa).

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Now you should not disregard me. Protect me completely. He speaks with humility. I am suffering from the experience of sins in saṁsāra (iha) for a long time, suffering from lamentation after exhaustion of pious results. Or I am suffering from sinful karmas (vṛjinaiḥ) and actions of lust at the present moment (anutāpaiḥ). This means external and internal suffering. I have no peace at all, by which I can have steadiness and happiness. I have attained closeness (upeta) to your feet directly (sam) or in an indescribable manner with revelation of your form, without my endeavor (kathaṣcit). O giver of shelter! You give shelter according to your promise. Ārtānāṁ śaraṇaṁ tv aham: I am the shelter for the sufferers. (SB 11.26.33) You should not say that shelter is dependent on bhakti to you since you are the inspiration for bhakti. Parātman! You give impetus everywhere. You should give according to the glory of your lotus feet at this time, and nothing else. His feet are described with this intention. Do not give lamentable liberation or Brahma’s abode, or yoga-siddhis which are subject to fear of time. Your feet give fearlessness, are most proper, and have no lamentation. Protect me who have attained you from danger or from all obstacles since you are compassionate to the miserable. He repeats that he has attained the Lord out of great pain. Only you can do this (īśa)! Or protect me so I have no fear, no lamentation and have truth (abhayam, aśocam, ṛtam). You never give anything unpleasant. O dearest one (parātman)! The Lord as the dearest has been described at the beginning of Chapter Fourteen. You must protect the person who has surrendered (āpannam). You should not have shame or fear in giving mercy to a low person. O Lord, supremely independent (īśa)!

    Personal Guidance
    For so long I have been pained, burning with lamentation; my six enemies — lust, anger, greed, illusion, pride, envy — are never satiated. Protect me, Supreme Soul; in danger I have come to You. Final petition uses both diagnosis and surrender.
    Reflection Questions
    • Which of the six inner enemies is most insatiable in you?
    • Could you take the same shelter Mucukunda takes today?
    Analogy

    The kṣatriya finally names his pain: long-burnt, six-enemied, never sated, never at peace — and now, by some good fortune, fallen at Your feet. The verse is bhakti's threshold-cry, the Vaiṣṇava-equivalent of 'sarva-dharmān parityajya' from the suppliant's side.

    Stories
    Gajendra's surrender

    In SB 8.2-3, the elephant-king Gajendra, gripped by the crocodile in the lake, finally exhausts his own strength and cries out — 'O original Person, supreme shelter, deliverer of those in danger, please save me.' Viṣṇu descends instantly on Garuḍa and rescues him.

    Mucukunda's verse 57 is the human-form parallel. Long suffering, the six enemies unsatiated, no peace, finally falling at the lotus feet of the Lord. Gauḍīyas read Gajendra-mokṣa and Mucukunda-stuti as the same prayer in two species — śaraṇāgati's anatomy is universal.

    Important Words
    • sārvabhauma — O emperor
      From sarva (all) + bhauma (earthly). The universal sovereign. Bhagavān restores Mucukunda's royal title at the very moment of his confessed renunciation — true sovereignty is what the bhakta has just become, having surrendered the false sovereignty.
    • matiḥ — mind, intelligence
      Same matiḥ word arcing through the chapter (verses 46, 53). Now Bhagavān names it 'vimala' and 'ūrjitā' — spotless and potent. The bhakta's matiḥ, refined by his own confession, is certified by the Lord Himself.
    • vimala — spotless
      From vi (away) + mala (impurity). The bhakti-purified intellect. Gauḍīyas read vimala-mati as the diagnostic of advanced sādhana — not absence of feeling, but feeling cleansed of self-reference.
    • ūrjitā — potent
      From ūrj — vital energy. The matiḥ is not only pure but strong. Gauḍīyas link ūrja to the rasa-energy of bhāva-bhakti; Mucukunda's prayer has shown both purity (verses 45-50) and energy (verses 55-57).
    • pralobhitasya — of (you) who were enticed
      Past participle of pra-√lubh — to entice. Bhagavān admits the entrapment was deliberate. Vaiṣṇava theology: the Lord tests not to discover (He knows) but to display the bhakta's quality.
    The Supreme Lord said: O emperor, great ruler, your mind is pure and potent. Though I enticed You with benedictions, your mind was not overcome by material desires.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The Supreme Lord said: O emperor, great ruler, your mind is pure and potent. Though I enticed You with benedictions, your mind was not overcome by material desires.
    Commentary

    Your intelligence is strong, not being moved here and there. (urjjita )

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    O king of all those ruling the world (sārvabhauma mahā-rāja)! Or, O emperor! O king! The repetition is for respect. Your words are those of the Lord himself. This shows the good nature of the Lord. Your mind is devoid of impressions of saṁsāra (vimala) and is endowed with bold nature in rasa (ūrjitā). The reason is that your mind is not overcome with objects of desire--from kingdom up to liberation--like persons afflicted with greed, because of the practice of bhakti. You have stated that you are fully surrendered in the previous verse. Your mind is fully preoccupied with bhakti.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    O king of all those ruling the world (sārvabhauma mahā-rāja)! O emperor! O king or person displaying all wealth internally and externally (mahārāja)! Or O great king among all rulers of the earth! Your intelligence is devoid of lust and other faults (vimala) and profound or bold (ūrjjitā). Your mind is not overcome or agitated by desires for enjoyment, desires other than me, or benedictions, of a most greedy person.

    Personal Guidance
    The Supreme Lord says: your mind is pure and potent; though I enticed you with benedictions, your mind was not overcome by material desires. The Lord tests with offered boons; saints pass by refusing them.
    Reflection Questions
    • What 'tests by benediction' are coming to you that look like opportunity?
    • Could refusing be the right answer to many of them?
    Analogy

    The Lord turns from receiver to authenticator: 'I tempted you with benedictions; your mind was not overcome.' The teacher who set the trap now praises the student for not falling. Vaiṣṇava pedagogy at its sharpest — the test is real, the praise is real, both are mercy.

    Important Words
    • ekānta-bhaktānām — of unalloyed devotees
      Compound: ekānta (single-pointed) + bhaktānām (of devotees). The Gauḍīya category — bhaktas whose devotion is unmixed with karma, jñāna, yoga. The Six Gosvāmīs' favorite category; their writings repeatedly invoke ekānta-bhakti.
    • apramādāya — for the sake of (showing) freedom from bewilderment
      From a (not) + pramāda (bewilderment) + āya (for the sake). The bhakta's apramāda is the chapter's specific virtue. Echoes Mucukunda's verse 49 contrast between pramatta (the materialist) and apramatta (the Lord).
    • dhīḥ — intelligence
      Same root as dhī-mate (verse 22). The bhakta's discriminating intellect — never diverted. Gauḍīyas treasure this as Bhagavān's own definition of bhakti's intellectual signature: stability under temptation.
    • āśīrbhiḥ — by blessings
      Instrumental of āśīs — blessing, benediction. The same varas Mucukunda refused. Bhagavān names the universal Vaiṣṇava category: ekānta-bhaktas are invulnerable to even āśīs.
    • bhidyate — is diverted
      Passive of √bhid — to split, divide. The bhakta's dhī does not split. Gauḍīyas read this as the structural opposite of the impersonalist who 'merges' — the bhakta does not merge, but neither does he divide; he remains undividedly oriented to Kṛṣṇa.
    Understand that I enticed you with benedictions just to prove that you would not be deceived. The intelligence of My unalloyed devotees is never diverted by material blessings.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Understand that I enticed you with benedictions just to prove that you would not be deceived. The intelligence of My unalloyed devotees is never diverted by material blessings.
    Commentary

    Know that by offering you benedictions, I am showing other worshipers how you will not be distracted (apramadaya) by such things. Or another meaning is: Know that you will not be distracted, because the intelligence of the devotee is never attracted to material enjoyment.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Understand that you, tempted by benedictions, would not deviate. The intelligence of my devotee, who is devoid of other worship and other desires, is not absorbed in material enjoyment. To show this I tempted you.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    You would not become insane or obstructed (apramattāya) by attainment of material benedictions. You would always be careful to ignore benedictions (apramattāya), because the intelligence of devotees is never pierced by benedictions. May you never be afflicted at any time by lack of bhakti.

    Personal Guidance
    Understand I enticed you with benedictions just to prove you would not be deceived; the intelligence of My unalloyed devotees is never diverted by material blessings. Even being tested is itself a testimony from the Lord.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where could a recent 'temptation' actually have been a Kṛṣṇa-administered exam?
    • How might passing tests build the testimony of your own devotion?
    Analogy

    Kṛṣṇa names the principle: 'I tempted you to display your freedom from delusion. The intelligence of My unalloyed devotees is never diverted by blessings.' Vaiṣṇava theology of the niṣkāma-bhakta — pure devotion is structurally invulnerable to bribery, even Bhagavān's.

    Important Words
    • yuñjānānām — of those engaging themselves
      Present participle of √yuj — to yoke. The yogīs who 'yoke' themselves. Gauḍīyas read this verse against aṣṭāṅga-yoga without bhakti: the yoking succeeds technically but fails ontologically — the vāsanās remain.
    • abhaktānām — of nondevotees
      Compound: a (not) + bhaktānām (devotees). The Bhāgavata's pointed distinction: even yogic accomplishment without bhakti is structurally incomplete. The verse is direct theology, not nuance.
    • prāṇāyāma-ādibhiḥ — by prāṇāyāma and other practices
      Compound: prāṇāyāma (breath-control) + ādibhiḥ (and others). The aṣṭāṅga-yoga technical vocabulary. Vaiṣṇavas honor these practices when they support bhakti (cf. SB 11.6.29) but refuse them as independent paths.
    • akṣīṇa-vāsanam — with vāsanās not eliminated
      Compound: a (not) + kṣīṇa (worn-out) + vāsanam (impressions, seed-desires). The technical word for the latent saṁskāras. Bhakti, Bhagavān is saying, is what actually exhausts them — not breath-control.
    • punaḥ-utthitam — again risen up
      Phrase: punaḥ (again) + utthitam (risen). The vāsanās come back. Gauḍīyas read this as the empirical observation that confirms theology: yogīs without bhakti repeatedly fall — Viśvāmitra, Saubhari, others. The Bhāgavata is full of such cautionary cases.
    The minds of nondevotees who engage in such practices as prāṇāyama are not fully cleansed of material desires. Thus, O King, material desires are again seen to arise in their minds.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The minds of nondevotees who engage in such practices as prāṇāyama are not fully cleansed of material desires. Thus, O King, material desires are again seen to arise in their minds.
    Commentary

    Other worshippers however, are attracted to material enjoyment. That is illustrated in this verse. Of those who are not devotees, that is yogis and jnanais, by practice of pranayama , sama, dama etc., attraction to material enjoyment (uthitam) again is seen.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Those who engage in other practices to give up desire will deviate. Those who have attained samādhi (yuṣjānānām) do not rid their minds of desire for enjoying objects (akṣīṇa-vāsanam) since they lack bhakti which creates steadiness in the mind.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    One should not say that by aṣṭāṅga-yoga with mind in samādhi, the mind will not be agitated by benedictions. The mind of persons devoid of bhakti, engaged in yoga, develop desires. Or though they give up objects because of lack of bhakti, the impressions of objects does not decrease. O king, you can understand this. Or in this birth as a king, by protecting the devatās as part of a king’s duty, and even after sleeping a long time, bhakti did not arise. In another birth you will attain bhakti. However he actually had bhakti. That is explained in verse 14. Otherwise the Lord would not show such mercy to him.

    Personal Guidance
    The minds of nondevotees doing prāṇāyama are not fully cleansed of material desires; thus desires are seen to arise again. Discipline without devotion leaves the desire-tank refilling.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where have you noticed disciplines without devotion failing to purify?
    • Could devotion be added explicitly to the disciplines you already maintain?
    Analogy

    Bhagavān names the alternative: nondevotees engaged in prāṇāyāma and other yogic practices keep their material desires un-cleansed; the vāsanās rise again. Bhakti alone burns the seed. The verse is the chapter's quiet polemic against yoga-without-bhakti.

    Important Words
    • vicarasva — wander
      Imperative of vi-√car. Same root as verse 27 (Bhagavān walking on the cave's thorny floor). The freedom to wander, once Bhagavān's alone, is now the bhakta's. Bhagavān's prerogatives become the bhakta's after surrender.
    • mayi-āveśita-mānasaḥ — with mind fixed in Me
      Phrase: mayi (in Me) + āveśita (fixed) + mānasaḥ (mind). The technical Bhāgavata phrase for ekāgra-cit. Gauḍīyas read āveśa as the bhakti-form of samādhi — not absorbing-into-Brahman, but absorbing-into-Kṛṣṇa-as-Person.
    • bhaktiḥ — devotion
      From √bhaj — to share, partake. The Bhāgavata's central virtue. Bhagavān names what He grants by its proper name — bhakti, not jñāna or yoga or mokṣa. Mucukunda's path is named, not generic.
    • anapāyinī — unfailing
      From an (not) + apāyinī (going away). Devotion that does not desert. Gauḍīyas treasure this adjective: nitya bhakti, never lost. The opposite of the vāsanā that re-rises (verse 60); bhakti, once granted, anapāyinī.
    • nityadā — always
      From nitya — eternal. Echoes anapāyinī. Bhagavān is doubling the eternity-language: 'always, unfailing.' The verse is Kṛṣṇa's promise-grammar at its strongest.
    Wander this earth at will, with your mind fixed on Me. May you always possess such unfailing devotion for Me.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Wander this earth at will, with your mind fixed on Me. May you always possess such unfailing devotion for Me.
    Commentary

    I have already given you pure bhakti, but today I am giving it to you again.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    You will be successful. With your mind absorbed in me, wander as you will, since you will have unfailing bhakti to me at all times. Another version has yathāsti. This means tathāsti.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    “How can I develop bhakti?” Fix your mind on me at your will (kāmam), serving my lotus feet. Wander in a special manner (vicarasva), alone or associating with devotee, chanting my name. You will have causeless or continuous bhakti (anapāyinī) since your devotion is exclusive. Another version has astu. This is a blessing since pure bhakti is very rare, especially while wandering about.

    • UM SB 10-51-61 - Mind on Krishna - 2024-05-27 Hillsborough
      Her Grace Urmila Mataji· 2024-05-27· English
    Personal Guidance
    Wander this earth at will, with your mind fixed on Me; may you always possess such unfailing devotion. Freedom of movement plus fixed devotion is the prescription for a liberated life.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where could you 'wander at will' while keeping your mind fixed?
    • What in your fixed routines might actually be flexible if mind stayed centered?
    Analogy

    Kṛṣṇa hands Mucukunda his vocation: 'Wander the earth at will, your mind fixed on Me; may your devotion to Me be unfailing.' The kṣatriya-asleep is now bhakta-awake, given license to move freely on the planet because his interior is fixed.

    Stories
    Nārada wandering with the vīṇā

    Nārada Muni, by Bhagavān's own grant, wanders the three worlds — earth, heaven, and the in-between — with his vīṇā, perpetually chanting Hari's names (SB 1.6, 1.9). His itinerary is governed only by his own choice, because his mind is fixed on the Lord. Wandering with mind fixed is one of bhakti's signature gifts.

    Mucukunda receives the same charter in this verse. The Bhāgavata's geography is generous: the bhakta is free to go anywhere because nowhere is alien to Bhagavān. The earth has been re-mapped around the Person.
